walkthroughs.body_html:
Families & Households — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Families & Households brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Families & Households.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between reliability and validity in research?
options: Reliable and valid mean the same thing — that the research is good.
Radical feminists oppose all women's rights.
Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.
Reliability is whether a method produces consistent results when repeated; validity is whether it actually measures what it claims to. A method can be reliable but invalid, or valid but unreliable.

mcqs.q: How does radical feminism differ from liberal feminism?
options: Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.

Radical feminists oppose all women's rights.
